figures.caption: Fig. 1. Schematic illustration of precursor-stoichiometry-driven composite-phase reconstruction in CP-LPSC-x. Regulation of the Li2S-P2S5-LiCl precursor ratio generates a composite sulfide electrolyte consisting of a Cl-rich LPSC-like matrix, a P2S6 4−-containing thiophosphate secondary phase, and LiCl, thereby promoting Li+ transport, electrolyte densification, reduced electronic conductivity, and high-voltage cathode-side interfacial stability. 2

Fig. 2. Phase evolution and thiophosphate-framework reconstruction regulated by local stoichiometry in CP-LPSC-x electrolytes. (a) XRD patterns of nominal Li6- xPS5-xCl1+x samples with x = 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7. The enlarged region highlights the evolution of non-argyrodite secondary-phase reflections and LiCl-related reflections, marked by asterisks and triangles, respectively. (b) Raman spectra and the enlarged region showing the evolution of the P2S6 4−-related band. (c,d) S 2p and P 2p XPS spectra showing the composition-dependent evolution of PS4 3−-related and P2S6 4−-related species. (e) Relative peak-area fractions of PS4 3−-related and P2S6 4−-related species extracted from the S 2p and P 2p XPS fitting results. 3

Fig. 3. Densification behavior, transport properties, and local structural evolution of CP-LPSC-x electrolytes. (a-c) Surface SEM images of cold-pressed LPSC, CP- LPSC-0.1, and CP-LPSC-0.5 electrolyte pellets prepared at 500 MPa. (d) Nyquist plots of CP-LPSC-x electrolytes with x = 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7 at 30 ◦C. (e) Ionic and electronic conductivities of the CP-LPSC-x series at 30 ◦C. (f) Arrhenius plots of ionic conductivity measured from 40 to 80 ◦C. (g) 7Li MAS NMR spectra of LPSC and CP-LPSC-0.5. (h) 31P MAS NMR spectra of LPSC and CP-LPSC-0.5, showing the retained Cl-rich LPSC-like phosphorus environment and the emergence of P2S6 4−-related phosphorus environments in CP-LPSC-0.5. 4

Fig. 4. Electrochemical performance of all-solid-state cells assembled with a Li–In alloy anode, a single-crystal NCM811 composite cathode, and either LPSC or CP- LPSC-0.5 as the solid electrolyte. (a) Initial charge-discharge profiles at 0.1C with an upper cutoff voltage of 4.3 V vs. Li+/Li. (b) Corresponding dQ dV−1 profiles during the initial charge-discharge process. (c) Long-term cycling performance at 0.5C under a 4.3 V cutoff voltage. (d) Long-term cycling performance at 1C under a 4.3 V cutoff voltage. (e) EIS spectra collected after 100 cycles. (f) Rate performance from 0.1C to 3C and subsequent recovery at 0.1C. (g) Long-term cycling per­ formance at 1C under a 4.5 V cutoff voltage. (h) Comparison of initial discharge capacity at 1C and capacity retention after 500 cycles at 1C for the CP-LPSC-0.5- based cells and representative reported sulfide-electrolyte-based all-solid-stat

Fig. 5. Dynamic interfacial kinetics and Li+ transport behavior of all-solid-state cells assembled with a Li–In alloy anode, a single-crystal NCM811 composite cathode, and either LPSC or CP-LPSC-0.5 as the solid electrolyte. (a,b) Operando EIS spectra collected during the initial charge-discharge process. (c,d) Two- dimensional DRT heat maps converted from the operando EIS data, showing the evolution of impedance contributions over different relaxation-time regions as a function of cell voltage. (e) GITT voltage profiles. (f) Apparent Li+ diffusion coefficients derived from the GITT measurements as a function of state of charge. (g) State-of-charge-dependent internal resistance extracted from the GITT profiles. 7

Fig. 6. Cathode-side interfacial chemical evolution and structural integrity of composite cathodes in LPSC-based and CP-LPSC-0.5-based all-solid-state cells. (a,b) The S 2p and P 2p XPS spectra collected from the cathode side after cycling. (c) SEM and BSE images of LPSC-based and CP-LPSC-0.5-containing composite cathodes before cycling and after 100 cycles. (d,e) Raman spectra collected from the cathode side after the first charge and subsequent discharge. (f) High-resolution S 2p XPS spectra of the LPSC-based cell after charge to 4.5 V vs. Li+/Li and discharge to 2.8 V vs. Li+/Li. (g) High-resolution S 2p XPS spectra of the CP-LPSC-0.5-based cell after charge to 4.5 V vs. Li+/Li and discharge to 2.8 V vs. Li+/Li; S-SEE denotes the combined sulfide-electrolyte-derived sulfur contribution used for comparison with P2Sn-related species. examined at selected charge and discharge states [28]
